gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-imperia: Spaced-out and glossy, Stentiga looks expensive. Noto Sans Imperial Aramaic is the workhorse, its open-ended curves and modest capital height making plain text easy to settle into, while the heading saves its drama for display.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-inscrip: Wide-spaced and marker-soft, Stentiga feels polished but friendly. Noto Sans Inscriptional Parthian brings big open eyes on its e and a, and that generous, deep-bodied lowercase is the pair's best quality.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-jp: Noto Sans JP stands tall, with a lofty x-height and curves that sweep open. And Stentiga, with its stretched tracking and flat, swell-free corners, adds a polished, luxurious touch above it.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-kaithi: Noto Sans Kaithi fills each line with lowercase that nearly matches capitals. Its open-channeled e keeps things plain and approachable, and the body text can sit a touch larger than you'd expect beneath Stentiga's stout, widely tracked letters.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-kayah-l: Quiet and tidy, with brush ends that lift away before curves close, Noto Sans Kayah Li barely raises its capitals above the lowercase. Stentiga, meanwhile, spreads its uniform strokes wide and glossy, so display lines feel grand while the body stays low-key.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-kharosh: Noto Sans Kharoshthi runs thick and dark through each line, with curves that never fold back on themselves, while Stentiga holds a single pen width. Together the text feels dense yet friendly.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-khmer: Noto Sans Khmer reads with generous chisel-notch openings and small letters that stand almost capital-sized, which gives it a clean, modern presence. Stentiga's blunt marker tips and spaced-out tracking lead above, and paragraphs below feel steady.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-khojki: Noto Sans Khojki lets light through its wide exits. Stentiga is best at making a statement, with every stroke carrying the same visual weight, while the body font is best at large, clear e shapes that read quickly.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-khudawa: Approachable from the first line, with rounds left unlatched like open hooks. Noto Sans Khudawadi keeps capitals and lowercase close in height, so a long stretch of text feels smooth beneath Stentiga's pipe-cleaner letterforms.
gen-dafont-stentiga-gf-noto-sans-kr: Noto Sans KR reads big and open, with a tall x-height and stubby ascenders. Stentiga does its best work as a spaced-out, constant-ink headline, while the body font is better at generous curves that stay clear.
